review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp, norm_cast and simps attributes. I also grepped Mathlib for uses of lp.coeFn_single, lp.coeFn_sum and lp.single_apply. I did not run Lean, so the findings are about missing or inconsistent simp coverage, not observed simplifier behaviour. I found no rewrite cycles or competing rules. lp.norm_single is simp with a side condition 0 < p, which looks fine. lp.star_apply is probably redundant next to coeFn_star, but that is a minor point and I did not report it. I report two findings, both about unapplied coercion lemmas that are missing from the simp set.

findings.excerpt:
@[norm_cast]
protected theorem coeFn_single (p) (i : α) (a : E i) :
    ⇑(lp.single p i a) = Pi.single i a := rfl
findings.problem: The applied form `lp.single_apply` is `@[simp]`, but the unapplied coercion form `⇑(lp.single p i a) = Pi.single i a` is only `@[norm_cast]`. So `simp` can rewrite `lp.single p i a j` but not `⇑(lp.single p i a)` when it is not applied, for example inside a sum or inside `‖·‖`. The same file lists it by hand in `simp only [lp.coeFn_single, coeFn_sum, ...]` in `norm_sum_single`, `norm_single` and `norm_sub_norm_compl_sub_single`. The same pattern appears in `l2Space.lean` (`simp_rw [lp.coeFn_single]`). All the neighbouring coercion lemmas (`coeFn_zero`, `coeFn_neg`, `coeFn_add`, `coeFn_sub`, `coeFn_smul`) are simp, so this is an inconsistent gap.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp, norm_cast]`. Orientation is fine: the RHS is the standard `Pi.single` normal form, which already has simp lemmas such as `Pi.single_eq_same`, `Finset.sum_pi_single` and `Pi.single_zero`. This also makes `lp.single_apply` derivable from it plus `Pi.single` rewriting. Then drop the explicit `lp.coeFn_single` from the `simp only` calls where it is no longer needed.
findings.benefit: Goals involving `⇑(lp.single p i a)` can be closed by plain `simp`. Proofs such as `norm_sum_single` and `inner_single_left` no longer need to name the lemma by hand. The simp normal form is the same for the applied and unapplied coercion.

evidence.excerpt: lp.single p i a j = Pi.single i a j

findings.excerpt:
theorem coeFn_sum {ι : Type*} (f : ι → lp E p) (s : Finset ι) :
    ⇑(∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, ⇑(f i) :=
findings.problem: `coeFn_sum` is the only coercion-pushing lemma in this block without `@[simp]`. `coeFn_zero`, `coeFn_neg`, `coeFn_add`, `coeFn_sub`, `coeFn_smul` and `coeFnAddMonoidHom_apply` are all simp. As a result, `simp` normalises `⇑(f + g)` but stops at `⇑(∑ i ∈ s, f i)`. The file then lists it by hand in `simp only [..., coeFn_sum, ...]` in `norm_sum_single` (line 1090) and `hF'` (line 1159), and in `norm_sub_norm_compl_sub_single` (line 1154).
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`. The direction is the same as the existing `Finset.sum_apply`, and the summation index set shrinks or stays the same, so there is no loop risk. The RHS is a Pi-sum of coercions, which `Finset.sum_apply` handles when it is applied.
findings.benefit: The simp set becomes consistent for finite sums in `lp`. Proofs about sums of `lp.single` no longer need the lemma named explicitly.
